title: 6 Mech / 6 Goblin Legendary Hunt

sources.label: HOW TO FIND ANY ★★★ Legendary Units This Way! HYPER 6 Mech Build!

body:
# 6 Mech / 6 Goblin Legendary Hunt

This is less a fixed comp than an engine for manufacturing Legendaries. The
whole plan hangs on the Mech class perk, *Heart of the Machine*: with six
different Mech (Inventor) pieces on the board, every home battle you win —
so long as one Mech survives — hands you a **Golden AWESOME Invention**, which
lets you discover a panel of five random Legendary units. Stack Goblin over the
top for cheap, unkillable early-game bodies and you have a board that both wins
consistently and prints five-cost pieces round after round. It is a high-skill,
slightly hit-or-miss line, but when it lands you three-star Legendaries far
ahead of the lobby.

## The relic engine

Two relics turn the discover-Legendaries plan from "nice" into "degenerate":

- **Wheel of Wonder** — a one-shot relic that grafts a synergy tag of your
  choice onto a unit. Because Mech and Goblin are the tags you actually need,
  you park it on a Wizard (Rubick or Naga Siren) and use it to fill your last
  Mech slot, freeing a board space. Wizards are also never targeted first, so
  it is a safe home for it.
- **Magic Box** — best taken *after* round 20. Roll up any Legendary you
  don't want, buy it, and Magic Box re-rolls it into a different Legendary.
  Combined with the five-gold "first to discover" bounty, you cycle the entire
  Legendary pool into exactly the pieces you're hunting.

Rough plan: look for Wheel of Wonder at the round-10 relic, Magic Box at
round 20.

## Core Units

Six Goblins and six Mech overlap heavily, so a ten-piece level-9/10 board
covers both at once.

| Unit | Cost | Tags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Techies | 5 | Goblin, Mech |
| Gyrocopter | 5 | Dwarf, Mech |
| Timbersaw | 2 | Goblin, Mech |
| Clockwerk | 1 | Goblin, Mech |
| Tinker | 1 | Goblin, Mech |
| Meepo | 2 | Kobold, Mech |
| Bounty Hunter | 1 | Goblin, Hunter |
| Alchemist | 4 | Goblin, Ogre, Warlock |
| Warlock | 5 | Orc, Warlock (Legendary damage) |
| Spectres | 5 | Demon Hunter, Undead (Legendary damage) |

Techies is the jackpot pickup — it is a Goblin *and* a Mech in one body, so it
counts toward both bonuses simultaneously. Gyrocopter is the other reliable
Legendary damage dealer. Warlock (with Necronomicon) and Spectre are the
flexible slots you fill from your Golden Inventions; swap in Tidehunter, Wraith
King, or whatever the board hands you.

## Items

- **Vanguard, Tranquil Boots, Buckler** on an early melee Goblin — the classic
  cheap unkillable front line that carries the win streak.
- **Telescope + Refresher Orb** on Techies — Refresher doubles the bomb, and
  Telescope boosts its physical/AoE damage.
- **Mask of Madness + Radiance** on Gyrocopter — attack speed, lifesteal, and
  splash for the passive cannon.
- **Manta Style** on Spectre — illusions each carry Spectre's damage.
- **Necronomicon** on Warlock — extra summons stack with his golems.

## Relics

- **Wheel of Wonder** (round 10) — add a Mech tag to a Wizard to complete 6 Mech.
- **Magic Box** (round 20+) — re-roll unwanted Legendaries into the ones you want.
- **Doubloon** is a strong pickup on a win streak (high HP converts to a large
  gold injection).

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Play a Goblin win streak early: keep pairs, bank to 10+ gold for interest, and
let the cheap Goblin front line steamroll. Push to level 8, then 9, to raise
Legendary odds. Crucially, once you're winning with 6 Mech you stop rolling for
units almost entirely — leveling is what adds Legendaries to your pool, and the
free Inventions do your "rolling" for you. Save your Invention tokens (bank up
to two) so you can buy multiple Legendaries from a single panel.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Give your best defensive items to whatever survives — a dead Mech means no
Invention. Front-load your spellcasters (Tidehunter, Techies, Alchemist for the
armour shred) so they fire first. Wraith King wants your Legendaries clustered
within two tiles so his revive covers them. Against heavy-armour boards
(Goblins, Warriors) pivot toward four Demon Hunters (Spectre, Anti-Mage,
Terrorblade) to convert your damage to pure. The big late-game mistake to avoid:
after ~round 40, don't stubbornly stay on Goblin/Mech — by then you've collected
enough Legendaries to drop the enablers and field a pure Legendary board.
